name: LightCraft
description: Headless photo library and raw developer (LightCraft from ArtCraft, open source, written in Rust; a Lightroom alternative). Imports camera raws (DNG, Canon CR2/CR3, Nikon NEF, Sony ARW, Fujifilm RAF, Olympus ORF, Panasonic RW2, Pentax PEF), JPEG, TIFF, PNG and WebP, develops them non-destructively — exposure, white balance, tone, curves, color, detail, lens corrections, crop, presets and masks through 390 commands — renders previews and exports full-resolution JPEG, TIFF and PNG.
instructions:
LightCraft runs headless in your own container; every file lives in /work.

1. Upload the photo to /work and import it: import {"paths":["/work/IMG_0001.dng"]} returns its photo id (e.g. {"imported":[1]}); the last imported photo is the active one, the develop tools act on it (or pass "id").
2. Read the sliders and their current values: list_controls {"section":"light"} (also "color", "effects", "detail"…). Exposure is light.exposure in EV (-5..5); white balance is wb.temp in Kelvin (the as-shot value of the raw, 2000..50000) and wb.tint.
3. Develop: set_develop {"values":{"light.exposure":0.5}}. Warmer white balance = a higher wb.temp than the current value, e.g. +800 K: set_develop {"values":{"wb.temp":5350}}; cooler = lower. Presets: command_run {"id":"develop.wb","params":{"mode":"daylight"}} (also cloudy, shade, tungsten, fluorescent, flash, auto, asShot). Crop: crop {"rect":[x0,y0,x1,y1]} in 0..1 of the photo, optionally "angle". Everything else is an engine command: command_list {"filter":"develop"} (also "mask", "preset", "lens", "curve"…) — always pass a filter, the registry has about 390 commands — then command_run {"id":...,"params":{...}}, or command_batch {"steps":[...]} for several. get_develop shows all settings of the photo.
4. Check the result: render_preview {} saves a PNG of the developed photo into /work and returns its path (no inline image) — download it to look at it or to show it.
5. Export: export {"path":"/work/IMG_0001.jpg","quality":90,"longEdge":0}. Always pass "longEdge":0 for the full resolution — without a size the engine shrinks the long edge to 3000 px; for a smaller file pass "longEdge":2048 (or "width", "height", "percent"). The format follows the extension: .jpg, .tif (16-bit by default, "bitDepth":8 for 8-bit) or .png. Use a new file name for every export.
6. Hand the result over: download it from /work with plugin_download_file.

All paths must be inside /work; relative paths resolve against /work. The library lives in memory only: a new MCP session (e.g. after a reconnect) starts with an empty library. To keep the edits, command_run {"id":"photo.saveMetadataToFile"} writes an XMP sidecar next to each original in /work; importing the photo again later reads it back. The container and /work are deleted after the conversation is idle, so always download the results.

accepts.description: XMP sidecar with develop settings saved earlier, next to its photo

returns.description: Developed photo as PNG, or a render_preview PNG
XMP sidecar with the develop settings, to continue editing later
